h i g h l i g h t s

 A mathematical model is developed for carbon capture and storage (CCS) planning.
 The model considers both grid power implications and CO2 source-sink matching.
 The model determines optimal CO2 allocation for maximum emissions reduction.
 A realistic case study is solved to illustrate the proposed approach.

                                                                                            tainty in predicting the economic cost as well as life cycle-based
                                                                                            carbon intensity of CCS installations [48]. Part of the uncertainty

                                                                                            ﬁning the technology to be used to compensate for energy losses
                                                                                            resulting from CC retroﬁts. In this work, the effects of changes in
                                                                                            the emission factor and the cost of compensatory power on CCS
                                                                                            are analyzed to assess the robustness of the optimal results. As

                                                                                            5. Conclusion

                                                                                               A comprehensive model for CCS deployment has been devel-
                                                                                            oped in this paper. This model uniﬁes the problems of grid effects
                                                                                            of power plant retroﬁtting and the subsequent CO2 source-sink
                                                                                            matching. The need for additional power generation from new,
                                                                                            low-carbon plants to compensate for CC energy losses is also ac-
                                                                                            counted for. An illustrative case study was solved to demonstrate
                                                                                            the use of the model to realistic CCS planning problems. Sensitivity
                                                                                            analysis has been performed to show the interplay between carbon
                                                                                            emissions and power losses in the system. Further analyses were
                                                                                            also done to assess the effects of parametric uncertainties. In future
                                                                                            work, the model will be expanded to take into account detailed
                                                                                            schedule changes and electricity demand growth. Geographical as-
                                                                                            pects, network topology and capital cost considerations may also
                                                                                            be integrated in future variants. Finally, effects of technological
Fig. 13. Effects of increase in the CO2 intensity of compensatory power (C = 1.3).          learning on power costs may be integrated to account for the long
                                                                                            time horizon involved.
